title: Rectangle class
description: Write a class `Rectangle` whose `__init__(self, width, height)` stores both dimensions as attributes, and whose method `area(self)` returns the rectangle's area (`width * height`).
hints: The constructor needs to remember the width and height so other methods can use them later.
Inside `__init__`, assign incoming parameters to instance attributes with `self.attribute = value`.
Set `self.width = width` and `self.height = height` in `__init__`, then have `area` return `self.width * self.height`.
expected_behavior: Rectangle(width, height) stores width and height as attributes; calling .area() returns width * height.
explanation: `__init__` stores the constructor arguments as instance attributes `self.width` and `self.height`, so any method on the object can access them afterward. `area` simply multiplies those two attributes together to compute the rectangle's area.
